title: Hinduja Global Solutions Ltd - 532859 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: HGS Q1 FY27 revenue fell 3.2% QoQ to Rs 1,050.4 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 9.7% from 15.7%, with PAT at Rs -66.3 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 1,050.4 crore, down 3.2% sequentially and 0.6% year-on-year, as planned phase-outs of legacy contracts offset ramp-ups of new wins. EBITDA fell to Rs 116.3 crore (9.7% margin) from 15.7% in Q4, which management attributed to one-time phase-out costs and front-loaded investment in sales, solutioning, domain hiring and AI (Agent X). Net loss widened to Rs -66.3 crore, with PBT before exceptionals at Rs -52.8 crore. Management said the margin pressure is a one-time absorption rather than a structural change, and it expects revenue and margins to improve later in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs +14.1 crore QoQ and Rs -26.5 crore YoY
vs Rs -13.6 crore QoQ; year-ago Rs +11.2 crore included Rs 57.5 crore from discontinued operations

financial_highlights.value: Rs 5,326 crore (gross Rs 6,605 crore; borrowings Rs 1,279 crore)

financial_highlights.change: interest from Rs 48.1 crore QoQ; depreciation from Rs 134.9 crore QoQ

segments.name: CX services
segments.commentary: 54% of Q1 operating revenue, consistent with the FY26 mix.

segments.name: Digital and Media services
segments.commentary: 46% of Q1 operating revenue. Broadband (CelerityX enterprise, retail) growing; digital television (linear TV) under headwinds mitigated by bundling, IPTV and cost actions.

segments.name: Vertical mix
segments.commentary: Tech, Media and Telecom 46%, CG and Retail 19%, BFSI 17%, Public Sector 12% (mainly UK and Canada), Health and Life Sciences 3%, others 4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects operating leverage to return as volumes normalise and AI/platform investments commercialise; margin absorption described as near-term, medium-term margin accretive.
Revenue and margin growth expected to pick up before the end of FY27 as ramp-downs conclude, per CEO; ramp-downs expected to end before FY27 year-end.
New logos typically take 6 to 8 months to contribute meaningfully; initial engagements about $150,000 to $300,000; first 3 months carry training and ramp costs.
Management is cautiously optimistic, citing macro uncertainty and client prudence that may persist near term; priority is sustainable profitable growth.
Project Ganga moves into operational mode in Q2 FY27; reporting for it to change from end of Q2.
Pricing shift: intent to move a growing share of contract value to outcome-linked, non-headcount structures.
capex_capacity: Project Ganga (UP government digital inclusion, launched 9 June 2026) to connect over 2 million households over 2 to 3 years across 75 districts; funded primarily from internal accruals.
About 2,000 applications received on the Project Ganga portal by 4 August 2026; about 500 trained so far; target 8,000 to 10,000 Nyaya Panchayat entrepreneurs, 50% women.
Incorporated HGS MENA IT Consulting LLC in Dubai to build technology and consulting capabilities across MENA.
Investments in domain hiring, fractional advisors, solutions build-out, Agent X and platform services, expensed in Q1 ahead of revenue.
Broadband high-speed adoption (above 100 Mbps) rose to 15% of subscribers from 11% a year earlier; 10 to 30 Mbps entry plan share fell to 18% from 22%.
demand_pricing: Added 19 new logos across CX and digital services and 8 clients in HRO and payroll processing in Q1; about 78 to 79 new logos added in FY26.
Pipeline described as strong in agentic AI, process automation, contact center, digital modernization and platform services.
Lost contracts were largely labour-priced; new wins carry more technology content, offshore delivery and outcome-linked pricing, so margins expected to improve ahead of revenue.
New AI-enabled deals expected to shift 20% to 30% of work to AI, scaling to 60% to 70% over time; deals becoming multi-towered.
Clients slow to move from AI pilots to production due to data and governance readiness; management expects deployments to scale through FY27.
Project Ganga pricing set in line with competition in Uttar Pradesh; the programme is no profit, no loss on the enabler/handholding role, with ISP service economics unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What margins apply to Project Ganga, and is it a subsidised programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Vynsley Fernandes said HGS is enabler and knowledge partner; pricing is in line with Uttar Pradesh competition and the no profit, no loss stance applies to supporting network roll-out, not to the ISP business. He said it is not a negative cash flow play.

qa_highlights.question: How should the ramp-up of 19 new CX and digital logos be read for revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Venkatesh Korla said revenue typically starts 6 to 8 months after addition, with initial work around $150,000 to $300,000 and 3 months of training and onboarding costs; margins should be attractive before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is limiting faster revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination of planned ramp-downs (expected to end before FY27 year-end) and ramp-up time; new deals are smaller in revenue size with AI but higher in margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients moving from Agentic AI pilots to production?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is high but many customers are not yet ready on data and governance; management expects deployments to grow through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will success of Agent X be measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited number of customers and contracts with AI embedded and possibly tracking the share of revenue influenced by AI; it will take the question away to consider reporting.

qa_highlights.question: Are larger or more integrated deals emerging from intelligent experiences positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: every recent new deal has AI components, and deals are becoming multi-towered with data and analytics work that is expected to lift revenue and margins over time.

risks_watch: Q1 EBITDA margin of 9.7% and net loss of Rs -66.3 crore; watch whether margins recover in Q2 FY27 as one-time phase-out costs end.
Digital television (linear TV) headwinds in India and globally, mitigated by broadband bundling, IPTV and cost optimisation.
Project Ganga execution, reporting clarity from Q2 FY27, and KPIs (trainees, loans under CM YUVA scheme, networks rolled out, customers onboarded) promised for next quarter.
Pace of ramp-down of legacy contracts, which management expects to conclude before FY27 year-end.
Client readiness for agentic AI production deployments; macro uncertainty and client prudence may persist.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic overall: management frames the Q1 margin fall as deliberate one-time investment and transition cost, while acknowledging revenue is flat-to-down and client demand is prudent. Answers on Project Ganga pricing and AI monetisation were less specific, with AI revenue tracking deferred to a later date.
key_quotes: The impact on margins is immediate because of ramp and training costs.
Consistent with what we have said in our prior quarters, we view this as a one-time cost and investment phase absorption, rather than any structural change in our earning power.
Every offer we take to market comes with a 90-day proof of value and defined outcomes. If it does not work, the client does not pay for it.
We expect that to show in the margin structure ahead of revenue cycle in following quarters.

adds.what: Project Ganga (UP digital inclusion) to connect over 2 million households over 2 to 3 years across 75 districts; enabler/handholding role, not owned capacity

growth.why: Management gives only directional guidance that revenue and margin growth will pick up before end of FY27, with no numbers; backing is partial via 19 new logos, a strong pipeline, outcome-linked pricing and Project Ganga, but no specific capacity or contract values are quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 9.7% from 15.7% in Q4 on one-time phase-out costs and front-loaded investment; management says margins improve as new wins with outcome-linked pricing ramp, with new logos needing 6-8 months to contribute.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No owned capacity build is discussed; Project Ganga is an enabler/handholding role and the only physical footprint news is a Dubai consulting entity, so no new plant or line is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue fell 3.2% QoQ to Rs 1,050.4 crore and grew only 0.6% YoY, with 19 new logos and 8 HRO/payroll clients added in Q1 but ramp-downs continuing until FY27 year-end.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed beyond expensed investments in hiring and AI, and no utilisation figure is given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is directional only, with no numbers, and management is cautiously optimistic citing macro uncertainty and client prudence.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 PAT was Rs -66.3 crore and PBT before exceptionals Rs -52.8 crore, so the recovery depends on margins returning after one-time costs, and client prudence may persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agent X and AI platform services are being built out, but management has not set a launch date and the AI revenue tracking is deferred to a later date.

rows.label: Project Ganga digital inclusion rollout (UP)
rows.why: Programme moves to operational mode in Q2 FY27 to connect over 2 million households over 2-3 years across 75 districts, with about 2,000 applications and 500 trained so far, though it is a no profit, no loss enabler role.

rows.label: Shift to outcome-linked, non-headcount pricing
rows.why: Management intends to move a growing share of contract value to outcome-linked structures, and new wins carry more technology content, offshore delivery and outcome pricing, with margins expected to improve ahead of revenue.

rows.label: New AI-enabled deals and multi-towered work
rows.why: Added 19 CX and digital logos plus 8 HRO and payroll clients in Q1 (about 78-79 new logos in FY26), with each recent deal carrying AI components and initial engagements of $150,000-$300,000.

tone.note: Management was confident that the Q1 margin fall is a one-time absorption and that new AI-led logos will lift margins, but cautious on near-term revenue, client prudence, and deferred AI revenue tracking; analysts pushed on Project Ganga pricing and margins and how Agent X success will be measured.

oneOffs.what: One-time phase-out costs and front-loaded investment in sales, solutioning, domain hiring and AI (Agent X) cited for EBITDA margin drop to 9.7% from 15.7%
Year-ago PAT of Rs +11.2 crore included Rs 57.5 crore from discontinued operations, making the PAT comparison look better than the recurring business

quality.why: Revenue grew only -0.6% YoY (Rs 1,050.4 crore) and total income +1.2% YoY, so top-line growth is essentially flat; the brief attributes the margin collapse to one-time phase-out costs and front-loaded investment, and the year-ago PAT included Rs 57.5 crore from discontinued operations, so the reported PAT decline overstates the recurring deterioration.
